name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Hewlett Packard Enterprise logo 2025.svg)

description: HPE sells enterprise IT infrastructure: servers (ProLiant, Cray supercomputers and AI systems), networking (Aruba and, since the Juniper merger, Juniper), private-cloud and storage (GreenLake), and financing for customers' purchases. Servers are 51% of revenue but only 37% of segment profit; networking is 20% of revenue and 44% of segment profit at a 23% margin. A FY2025 goodwill impairment of $1.6 billion pushed GAAP operating margin to -1.3%. From FY2026 it reports Networking, Cloud & AI (servers, hybrid cloud and financing merged) and Corporate Investments and Other.

businessLines.name: Server
businessLines.how: One-time sales of ProLiant servers, Cray exascale and AI systems, backed by a global manufacturing-services footprint; revenue swings with average unit prices and large AI orders.

businessLines.name: Hybrid Cloud
businessLines.how: GreenLake private-cloud services, storage solutions and associated private cloud software, sold both as-a-service and as products (the 10-K does not split the mix).

businessLines.name: Networking
businessLines.how: Sells wired and wireless LAN, WAN routing, data-center networking, security and AIOps software (Aruba and Juniper); one distributor, about 10% of HPE revenue, buys mainly Server and Networking products.

businessLines.name: Financial Services
businessLines.how: Captive financing: leases and financing of HPE hardware, software and services so customers pay over time, earning lease and interest income.

businessLines.name: Corporate Investments and Other
businessLines.how: Advisory and professional services and other small businesses; the Communications Technology Group was sold to HCLTech effective 2024-12-01, cutting revenue 23.5%.
